description: We are looking for a Graduate / Junior StructuresEngineer to begin your career in rocket structures and grow quickly through hands-on responsibility. You will have the opportunity to develop across design, analysis, manufacturing, materials, and testing while working closely with experienced structural engineers. This role is designed for someone curious, practical, and eager to contribute wherever the team needs support. You will work with real hardware from day one and take on increasing ownership as your strengths and experience develop. About us We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, have just crossed €10m in revenue for our first operating year and are applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket. We are working hard to build something truly spectacular. To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you. At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Support the engineering of rocket structures, from geometry and modelling through to calculation and evaluation using CAD and FEA. Gain hands-on experience manufacturing and prototyping composite hardware using filament-winding machines and curing equipment. Help prepare and conduct structural tests and material-characterisation activities, including tensile testing, DSC, and microscopy. Process engineering data and automate repetitive tasks using Python where useful. Document methods, results, and technical decisions clearly. Work closely with senior engineers and take on increasing ownership as your skills develop. What we are looking for A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, structural, or materials engineering, or a Master’s degree currently in progress. A solid foundation in structural mechanics, materials science, or manufacturing processes. Hands-on experience from a student engineering team, particularly in rocketry, Formula Student, aerospace, or a similar practical environment. Genuine curiosity and a practical, quality-conscious mindset. Fluent English. The ability to learn quickly, work collaboratively, and contribute across design, analysis, manufacturing, and testing. Desirable experience Composite materials, filament winding, curing, or structural testing. CAD or FEA work through academic, personal, or extracurricular projects. Basic Python scripting for data processing or task automation. Working proficiency in German. Benefits and important information: We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent. Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success. Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas. Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday Free access to shared company housing Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week. We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger. Please submit applications in English Compensation: €60K – €65K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus • €60K – €65K • Offers Equity • Offers Bonus Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

description:
In a nutshell

Our Java teams in the Logistics domain make sure that our products travel all the way from the suppliers in our electronic vehicles, and arrive at our customers’ houses with a smile. From optimizing our routes, to making our drivers’ lives easier, to planning and executing all inbound and outbound products: there’s a wide range of products to work on. Through designing, developing, and testing new features, or improving the scalability and security of our platform: you’ll be owning a product together with your team, while finding yourself fully immersed in an engaging scaleup culture.

Tricks of the trade

  • Ownership: Take ownership of projects from concept to delivery, aligning technical solutions with business goals with a product engineering mindset
  • Problem solving: You see a problem, you tackle it with technology - with your users always in mind
  • Contribution: Design, test, evolve, and evaluate the systems that underpin our Logistics operations, offering a creative and analytical approach
  • Our Tech: Java 21/25 (Spring 6 with Spring Boot 3.5, Reactor, Immutables, Maven), React, Angular, RabbitMQ, Kafka, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Git, Docker, AWS, Helm, Terraform, Kubernetes, Vault, Datadog, Python 3.x

We’re looking for

  • You have a Master’s Degree (in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology, Computer Engineering or a related technical field) or equivalent experience.
  • You have a product mindset: you own and solve business problems through tech
  • You have 1-5 years of professional experience in programming and software development
  • You have a profound understanding of software development principles and are ready to have hands on backend and frontend alike
  • Your English skills are on point (no Dutch required)
  • You're based in or happy to relocate to the Netherlands*

* We work from our office in Amsterdam. Being present makes a genuine difference to your team and the work. There's flexibility to work from home when needed, but if remote or hybrid-first is what you're after, this probably isn't the right fit.

Please send your CV in English for complete consideration.

Picnic Perks

✍🏼 Mastery is a journey!

You’ll get plenty of opportunities to challenge yourself and grow, including the Picnic Tech Academy, Lunch & Learn sessions, and tailored soft skills training.

💡 Make a difference

You will work on real-world problems, seeing the impact of your work every day in our warehouses and in our satisfied customers. Plus, our fully electric vehicles and sustainable business model mean you’ll also be contributing to making the world a better place!

🫱🏼‍🫲🏾 Teamwork makes the dream work

With more than 80 nationalities across 3 countries, you’ll be part of a diverse company with plenty of cool stuff to get involved with, from board game evenings, to after-work drinks, to our company ski trip and more!

🍎 You are what you eat

You’ll get freshly prepared, healthy lunches and snacks (with plenty of vegetarian, vegan, and halal options). Coffee snob? Don’t worry, our amazing Picnic barista has you covered.

🚴🏽 Stay healthy

Mental health is important. As well as having the option to speak with Picnic colleagues who act as confidential advisors, our collaboration with OpenUp gives you easy access to professional psychologists, along with workshops and materials. There are plenty of sports communities and events to get involved with, from tennis to yoga, to climbing!

🔋 Attractive package

We offer competitive compensation and a pension plan that looks out for your future self, as well as 25 vacation days per year, so you can recharge your batteries

🌍 Benefits for expats

It can be daunting starting a new job AND moving to a new country. That’s why we offer lots of support for our many expat colleagues, if you want to find our relocation benefits, see here.

description: Research Engineer, Manipulation Data & Teleoperation — Zurich This role owns the data generation layer of Sereact's VLA stack: teleoperation systems and data collection infrastructure that feed Cortex, built from our Zurich research hub. About Sereact Sereact is a Series B embodied-AI company. Cortex, our VLA model, is deployed in live warehouse robotic cells across the EU and US. Zurich is our newest research hub, focused on the manipulation and control problems that sit underneath Cortex. The role This is a Research Engineer position. It is scoped to the data generation layer of the VLA stack: teleoperation hardware and software, retargeting pipelines that map human demonstrations onto robot hands, and the data collection infrastructure that feeds Cortex. It requires building the systems that produce the data those models train on, and working closely with the training team on what that data needs to look like. What you'll do Build and operate teleoperation systems for dexterous manipulation, including retargeting algorithms that map human hand and arm motion onto robot end-effectors Design and maintain scalable, UMI-style data collection hardware and software that other engineers at Sereact rely on Benchmark control and retargeting approaches using rigorous, human-factors-informed methodology Instrument and support the physical robots deployed in the Zurich hub, including day-to-day work on the control stack Work with the model-training team to define what data they need and close the loop on data quality Build tooling or infrastructure outside your immediate brief when it unblocks the wider team What you'll bring MSc (or equivalent, in progress) in robotics, mechanical engineering, or a closely related field, with a thesis or capstone project on manipulation, teleoperation, or retargeting Hands-on experience building a data collection device or system for robot learning (UMI or a comparable system), not just operating one someone else built Working knowledge of retargeting algorithms for mapping human input onto robot hands or end-effectors 1 to 2 years of combined research, internship, or industry experience in robotics, mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline Software and systems engineering skills strong enough to build and maintain infrastructure other engineers rely on, not only research-grade prototypes Comfortable working as an individual contributor in a small, still-forming team Nice to have A conference submission on manipulation, teleoperation, or retargeting where the candidate is an author (an MSc thesis submitted to a venue like CoRL counts; supervising a student team whose own work was later published does not) Teaching or TA experience in a robotics course Some exposure to large-model training, even without an independent training record A concrete example of building something outside the formal role brief because the team needed it Location: Zurich Area, Switzerland: This role is based in our Zurich office, offering a vibrant ecosystem for robotics and AI. What We Offer: Free meals at the workplace. Flexible working hours and the option to work from home when needed. Direct collaboration with founders and world-leading AI experts. Access to large-scale compute clusters and proprietary robotic datasets. A key role in shaping the future of embodied AI. Competitive compensation and a relocation package for the Zurich area Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow
